---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: ReceivableBuild RevenueCash Divergence
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(recch, at), 1))), RANK(SUB(TREND(WINSOR(RATIO(revt, at), 1), 5), TREND(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf, at), 1), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with increasing receivables while revenue productivity improves faster than operating cash-flow productivity should underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This corrects the RECCH sign convention by using NEG(recch), so high values correspond to receivable build rather than collection. The quality interaction focuses on a revenue-cash divergence: reported sales momentum is less credible when it is accompanied by weaker cash conversion.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: InventoryBuild PersistentCashWeakness
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(invch, at), 1))), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf, sale), 1), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with inventory accumulation and persistently weak operating cash margins should underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This corrects the INVCH sign convention by using NEG(invch), so high values indicate inventory build. Unlike a pure inventory-growth signal, it penalizes inventory accumulation only when sales are not being converted into durable cash flow.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: WorkingCapital EarningsSmoothing Gap
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), at), 1)), RANK(SUB(VOL(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf, at), 1), 5), VOL(WINSOR(RATIO(ni, at), 1), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with rising working-capital accruals and cash flows that are much more volatile than reported earnings should underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: High working-capital investment can be benign, but it is more suspicious when accruals appear to smooth volatile cash performance into stable reported earnings. The signal targets accounting smoothing rather than simply rediscovering the low-accrual or low-earnings-volatility effects separately.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: PayablesStretch MarginErosion
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(apalch, at), 1)), RANK(NEG(TREND(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 1), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms stretching payables while gross margins are deteriorating should underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Rising payables can temporarily support operating cash flow, but it is less likely to represent durable quality when core margins are weakening. The interaction flags firms where supplier financing may be masking declining operating economics.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: CleanWorkingCapital CashEarningsAlignment
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(ABS(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), at), 1)))), RANK(SUB(TREND(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf, at), 1), 5), ABS(SUB(TREND(WINSOR(RATIO(ni, at), 1), 5), TREND(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf, at), 1), 5))))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with little working-capital accrual distortion and improving cash earnings that align with reported net income should outperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The accrual leg rewards firms without large working-capital swings, reducing the chance that reported performance is driven by balance-sheet timing. The quality leg requires cash-flow improvement while penalizing a gap between cash-flow and net-income trends, identifying genuinely cash-backed earnings persistence.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: DepreciationAddback CashErosion
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(dpc, at), 1)), RANK(NEG(TREND(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dpc), sale), 1), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with high depreciation add-back dependence and deteriorating depreciation-adjusted cash margins should underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Operating cash flow can look healthier when it is mechanically supported by large noncash depreciation add-backs. If cash margins after removing those add-backs are declining, reported cash generation is less likely to represent durable operating quality.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
